basis: Tooth agenesis defines dental involvement; choroid calcification lacks evidence of functional ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: calcification alone does not establish damaging ocular disease; its precise anatomical location is also unclear.

basis: Congenital cardiac defects, acral skeletal abnormalities and neurodevelopmental impairment characterize the principal subtypes.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay and intellectual impairment are defining features across the principal cardioacrofacial dysplasia subtypes.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy; muscle weakness and wasting reflect denervation rather than direct skeletal muscle disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: frequent muscle atrophy is downstream of peripheral nerve damage, without evidence of direct muscle or skeletal disease.

basis: Optic atrophy occurs in 2/6 (~33%), esotropia in 4/6; fixed contractures in 1/3 and pectus deformity in 2/6 support skeletal involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed flexion contractures (1/3) and pectus carinatum (2/6) are structural locomotor abnormalities meeting the approximately 30% threshold.

basis: Renal dysplasia and limb/rib malformations define the syndrome; lethal pulmonary hypoplasia occurred in all three described infants.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: pulmonary hypoplasia caused fatal respiratory failure in 3/3 infants; it is a downstream manifestation of the defining renal and skeletal syndrome.

basis: Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; PDA and metatarsus adductus each have HPO frequencies of 80-99%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: metatarsus adductus is a structural foot deformity annotated in 80-99%; arthralgia and weakness alone would not suffice.

basis: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia with characteristic intellectual disability defines DMC and distinguishes it from Smith-McCort dysplasia.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a defining diagnostic feature, rather than an incidental complication of the skeletal dysplasia.

basis: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma involves blood or marrow; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 30-50%.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration causing hepatomegaly occurs in approximately 30-50% and represents direct tumour occupation.

basis: Inherited vitamin A metabolic disorder; night blindness and Bitot spots are characteristic ocular manifestations, typically >=30%; skin involvement frequency is unknown.

decisions.dermatologic: none: follicular hyperkeratosis is documented, but its frequency is unspecified and cannot confidently be placed at >=30% or treated as a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Splenic hairy cell leukemia is explicitly classified under lymphoma in this concept; spleen is a haematologic organ, with no digestive tract involvement established.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the supplied concept explicitly has a lymphoma parent, supporting the lymphoma mechanism axis alongside haematologic splenic disease.
